notes: Version 2.1.2 is a downstream documentary correction: no central Foundation theorem is replaced. An independent audit of the companion Bell paper (Quantum Reports, DOI 10.3390/quantum8020044) found its central implication false: non-injectivity of an observable projection does not by itself obstruct Bell factorisation, refuted by a finite Bell-local countermodel (uniform measure, fibres of size eight, deterministic local response functions, CHSH exactly zero), and its PR-box construction has empty support (the four parity constraints are jointly unsatisfiable). The companion-papers relation, the entanglement section's Bell subsection (retitled from 'Why Bell's factorisation assumptions do not apply' to 'What a Bell-factorisation result would require'), and the summary table's Bell row are retyped accordingly; the general no-go theorem and correct obstruction (absence of a setting-independent global coupling across measurement contexts) are now cited to a new companion paper.
